chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him: 'How did it come to be that the menstruating woman takes what is in the Masjid but does not place anything in it?' So he said: 'Because the menstruating woman has the ability to place what is in her hand elsewhere, but she does not have the ability to take what is in it [the Masjid] except from it [what is with her to place it].'
ai.seo_question: Why can a menstruating woman take items out of the Masjid but not place them inside?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) provides a logical rationale for the juristic distinction between a menstruating woman entering and exiting the Masjid versus placing items within it. The ruling hinges on the physical capability of the woman: she can easily remove objects from the sacred space without her body touching the ground, but placing items down requires her to be present in a way that affects the space's purity status. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical feasibility ('istita'ah') as a determinant for legal obligations and prohibitions.
